set.body:
Phase D (architecture).

core/Batch.scala is 602 lines — the largest file in core, roughly 18% of the module — and contains axes (:13), grids (:20) with 2- and 3-ary cross products (:38,:41), an Argument opaque type (:51), an ArgValue typeclass with 6 instances plus enum derivation (:97-118), ScriptArguments with Mirror.ProductOf derivation (:125-191), language command prefixes bash/python3/rscript (:194-223), sharding (:269,:301,:486-524), gang plans (:282,:450-484) and batch topology (:306-330), plus BatchPlanner (:338-602).

These are valuable workflow facilities. They are not the scheduler kernel.

Move to slurm4s-batch (or task-oriented modules). Core retains ONLY: validated Slurm identifiers; resources and placement intent; launch specification; job/array-element identity; reported state and evidence; submit/query/cancel result models; Scheduler[F].

Also fix while extracting — Grid.product eagerly materializes and reports Int size:
    def size: Int = rows.length.toInt                                  // :21
    def product[B](other: Grid[B]): Grid[(A, B)] =
      Grid(rows.flatMap(left => other.rows.map(right => left -> right)))  // :26-29
Two 100k-row grids produce a 10^10-element flatMap: OOM with no typed BatchPlanFailure. Note the careful Int.MaxValue overflow guard already applied to RESOURCES at :584-594 — the row count itself gets none. Make it lazy, size Long, with an overflow guard.

Constraint: the move must preserve ONE lowering representation. Do not introduce separate batch and task IRs. Blocked by P8.D1, which defines that representation.
set.title: P8.D7: Extract batch and workflow facilities from core
